originalTitle: Abdul El-Sayed’s Michigan primary victory is the latest win for progressives challenging establishment-backed Democrats – live
summary: The former public health official’s victory in Michigan US Senate primary race comes after progressive wins in New York and Colorado
content: Rumors that Marjorie Taylor Greene, the former Maga congresswoman from Georgia, was about to announce the creation of a new political party with fellow exiles from the Trumpist movement, including Tucker Carlson, Thomas Massie and Joe Kent, appear to have been greatly exaggerated. However, the former congresswoman did unveil a different new venture this week: a Cameo account, where, for $150, her fans can now book Greene to deliver “unforgettable” video messages for friends or relations celebrating “a milestone birthday, an anniversary, or a long-awaited reunion”. Robert F Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services has provided a copy of Dr Anthony Fauci’s phone to a Republican-led Senate panel investigating the doctor’s role as a senior advisor on the response to the Covid-19 pandemic to presidents Donald Trump and Joe Biden, the Wall Street Journal reports. Kennedy, a lawyer with no scientific training, wrote a conspiratorial, 500-page book attacking Fauci in 2021 that sold more than a million copies for a rightwing publisher – thanks in part to blurbs from fellow non-scientists Tucker Carlson, Joe Rogan, Alan Dershowitz and Tony Robbins. The chair of the Senate panel, Republican Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, confirmed the report on social media. “Hopefully, this device will address many of the questions he refused to answer at last week’s hearing,” Johnson added. While delivering remarks, in English and French, about a drive to build affordable housing in Toronto on Wednesday, Canada’s prime minister broke off from his prepared remarks to say: “I would now like to inform you that ‌the teleprompter has ceased to function.” As the audience laughed, Carney ad-libbed a jibe about Donald Trump. “Unlike a certain world leader, I do not view this as a conspiracy,” the prime minister said, to more laughter. Last year, after his address to the United Nations general assembly was marred by technical mishaps – including a malfunctioning escalator, sound system and teleprompter – Trump suggested that he had been the victim of “triple sabotage at the UN”. Later in the event, Carney also said that Canadian trade negotiators were talking with US counterparts to find some way to avoid the implementation, in two weeks, of new tariffs imposed by Trump on a broad range of imports from Canada, on everything from alcohol and cement to hockey sticks. Carney’s mockery of Trump on Wednesday was not the first time he has made fun of the American president. Speaking in Ireland in June, Carney did a brief impression of Trump as he joked about having been presented with a ceremonial key to the White House during a visit to Washington. Moments after Nevada’s Republican governor, Joe Lombardo, stepped off stage at the midterm campaign rally hosted by Donald Trump on Wednesday, the president praised an election conspiracy theorist who is running to oversee Nevada’s elections as its secretary of state, Jim Marchant. The transition was awkward because Marchant won the Republican nomination for the office in June, narrowly defeating a candidate endorsed by Lombardo who is not an election-denier. “A very special man, I wish you’d get him in office, because he’s incredible, I’ve known him so long and he’s got to get in, he just has to,” Trump said. “He had a big victory with spending very little money because everyone respects him, Jim Marchant, he’s a candidate for secretary of state.” Marchant, who has spread baseless conspiracy theories about election fraud in Nevada for years, and previously said he would not have certified Joe Biden’s 2020 victory in the state, is attempting to unseat the Democratic incumbent, Cisco Aguilar, in a rematch of the 2022 election the Democrat won by just 23,000 votes. Jon Ralston, the chief executive of the non-profit Nevada Independent, noted with amazement Trump’s endorsement of “an unhinged conspiracy theorist who said he didn’t even trust the results of his own primary he won”. In a speech laced with anti-Muslim animus, Donald Trump just accused Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for the US Senate from Michigan, who is Muslim, of being motivated by deep-seated antisemitism. El-Sayed, who narrowly won the Democratic primary in Michigan despite $30m in negative ads paid for by groups linked to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac), has campaigned with Jewish supporters, but strongly condemned Israel’s killing and mistreatment of Palestinians. According to Trump, El-Sayed is “a hater of Jews and a hater of Israel”. “Just say this guy hates Jews. Somebody said, ‘Oh, that’s a little strong.’ No, he hates Jews and he hates Israel,” Trump said. “He’s a man of hate.” The president then mockingly pronounced El-Sayed’s name, clearly stressing its Arabic origins, eliciting boos from his supporters in Nevada, just as his earlier reference to “Barack Hussein Obama” had. At another point in the speech, Trump also made a sarcastic reference to “the lovely Islamic Republic of Iran”. Earlier on Wednesday, as other Republicans released frankly racist statements attempting to cast El-Sayed as a Muslim extremist, El-Sayed addressed Jewish Americans in comments carried live by Fox News. “To my Jewish American sisters and brothers, one of the most indelible memories of this campaign will have been the opportunity to break bread with you at seder,” El-Sayed said, “and listening to sisters and brothers who said, ‘I want to join this movement because Aipac doesn’t speak for me; because I understand that self-determination for one people does not require the quenching of self-determination for another people; that unless all of us are free, none of us are free,’ I want to tell you the great gift that you’ve given me.” “I want you to know,” he continued, “that my commitment to your safety, my commitment to Jewish safety, is the same commitment that I have to the safety of my own daughters.” Apparently referring to these comments, which were carried live on the president’s favorite networ

chineseContent: 有传言称，佐治亚州前马加国会女议员马乔里·泰勒·格林 (Marjorie Taylor Greene) 即将宣布与塔克·卡尔森 (Tucker Carlson)、托马斯·马西 (Thomas Massie) 和乔·肯特 (Joe Kent) 等特朗普运动流亡者一起创建一个新政党，但这一传闻似乎被过分夸大了。然而，这位前国会女议员本周确实推出了一个不同的新项目：一个 Cameo 账户，现在只需花费 150 美元，她的粉丝就可以预订格林，为朋友或亲戚传递“难忘”的视频信息，庆祝“里程碑式的生日、周年纪念日或期待已久的团聚”。据《华尔街日报》报道，罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的卫生与公众服务部已向共和党领导的参议院小组提供了安东尼·福奇博士的手机副本，该小组正在调查该医生作为唐纳德·特朗普和乔·拜登总统应对 Covid-19 大流行的高级顾问的角色。肯尼迪是一位没有受过科学训练的律师，他在 2021 年写了一本攻击福奇的阴谋论书，长达 500 页，为一家右翼出版商售出超过 100 万册，这在一定程度上要归功于非科学家塔克·卡尔森、乔·罗根、艾伦·德肖维茨和托尼·罗宾斯的介绍。参议院小组主席、威斯康星州共和党人罗恩·约翰逊在社交媒体上证实了这一报道。 “希望这个设备能够解决他在上周听证会上拒绝回答的许多问题，”约翰逊补充道。周三，加拿大总理用英语和法语发表了关于推动在多伦多建造经济适用房的讲话，但他中断了准备好的讲话，说道：“我现在想通知您，提词器已停止工作。”当观众大笑时，卡尼即兴嘲笑唐纳德·特朗普。 “与某个世界领导人不同，我不认为这是一个阴谋，”该公关
